commit_message:
avfilter/avf_showcqt: rewrite showcqt and add features

add yuv444p, yuv422p, and yuv420p output format (lower cpu usage
on ffplay playback because it does not do format conversion)
custom size with size/s option (fullhd option is deprecated)
custom layout with bar_h, axis_h, and sono_h option
support rational frame rate (within fps/r/rate option)
relaxed frame rate restriction (support fractional sample step)
support all input sample rates
separate sonogram and bargraph volume (with volume/sono_v and
volume2/bar_v)
timeclamp option alias (timeclamp/tc)
fcount option
gamma option alias (gamma/sono_g and gamma2/bar_g)
support custom frequency range (basefreq and endfreq)
support drawing axis using external image file (axisfile option)
alias for disabling drawing to axis (text/axis)
possibility to optimize it using arch specific asm code

Signed-off-by: Michael Niedermayer <michael@niedermayer.cc>

findings.title: Negative index in fft_data array write when step exceeds fft_len
findings.message: In filter_frame(), the index j is computed as s->fft_len - s->remaining_fill (later changed to s->fft_len/2 + s->remaining_fill_max - s->remaining_fill by a subsequent commit). After processing a CQT frame, s->remaining_fill is set to step, where step = sample_rate / (fps * count). When timeclamp and/or fps are low, fft_len can be small relative to step (e.g., timeclamp=0.01 at 44100Hz gives fft_len=512, while fps=15 count=5 gives step=588). This makes j negative (512 - 588 = -76). The subsequent loops iterate starting at m=0, writing to s->fft_data[j+m] with negative indices, causing heap buffer overflow (writes before the allocated buffer). This corrupts heap metadata, leading to SIGSEGV crashes, double-free errors, malloc assertion failures, and corrupted double-linked list errors depending on what memory is overwritten. The rewrite commit introduced this by changing fps from a bounded integer (10-100) to AV_OPT_TYPE_VIDEO_RATE with no practical lower bound, and removing the rate%(fps*count)==0 divisibility check, allowing step to exceed fft_len.
findings.suggestion: Clamp the loop start index to ensure j+m is never negative. Replace 'for (m = 0; ...' with 'for (m = FFMAX(0, -j); ...' in both loops that write to s->fft_data[j+m].

ground_truth.root_cause: The rewrite of showcqt in commit f8d429e0c56 relaxed the fps parameter from a bounded integer (10-100) to an unbounded VIDEO_RATE type and removed the divisibility check (rate % (fps*count) == 0). This allowed configurations where the step size (sample_rate / (fps * count)) exceeds fft_len (2^ceil(log2(sample_rate * timeclamp))). After the first CQT plot, remaining_fill is set to step, and on the next loop iteration j = fft_len - remaining_fill becomes negative. The loop starting at m=0 then writes to fft_data at negative offsets, corrupting the heap. A subsequent commit (c4a3526b57d) further lowered the timeclamp minimum from 0.1 to 0.002, making the bug much easier to trigger with moderate fps values.
